data.title: BlincVision signs evaluation agreement in industrial automation
data.description:
BlincVision has signed an evaluation agreement with a Swedish industrial company. The evaluation will explore how BlincVision’s high-speed sensor technology can be used in industrial automation to improve production flows and strengthen quality control.

The customer is a Swedish industrial company with manufacturing operations in Sweden and Germany, supplying solutions to industries including automotive and defence. The company has developed its own AI-based solutions that use cameras to identify and classify different components. As part of the evaluation, the companies will explore whether BlincVision’s sensor technology can improve performance in the customer’s industrial applications.

“Industrial automation is an interesting area for our technology. The ability to quickly identify and analyse what is happening in a production flow can contribute to both higher efficiency and quality. Together with the customer, we now have the opportunity to evaluate our technology in a real industrial environment and see where it can create the most value,” says Markus Johansson, CEO of BlincVision.

The evaluation is part of BlincVision’s work to expand the use of its technology across different markets and applications.

For more information, please contact:

Markus Johansson, CEO

E-mail: markus.johansson@blincvision.com

About BlincVision AB (publ)

The company develops the groundbreaking sensor solution BlincVision. The solution enables vehicles and machines to react earlier in high-risk situations. The technology focuses on relevant changes in the field of view, allowing faster detection. The ambition is to contribute to increased safety in environments where rapid decisions are critical, from urban traffic to applications within autonomous mobility, defense and industry.

BlincVision is headquartered in Lund, Sweden, and also operates in Gothenburg.

The company is listed on Nasdaq First North Premier Growth Market.

Follow our journey at blincvision.com.

Pollen Street Group Limited (the "Company")

INTERIM DIVIDEND DECLARATION

On 15 September 2026, the Directors of Pollen Street Group Limited declared an interim dividend of 28.5 pence per ordinary share for the period ending 30 June 2026 ("Interim 2026 Dividend").

The Interim 2026 Dividend will be paid on 23 October 2026 to holders of ordinary shares on the register as of 25 September 2026. The ex-dividend date is 24 September 2026. The Interim 2026 Dividend is the dividend declared in relation to the 6-month period ending 30 June 2026. As at Tuesday, 15 September 2026, being the declaration date of the Interim 2026 Dividend, the Company had 64,209,597 ordinary shares in issue, of which 5,186,413 ordinary shares were held in Treasury.

The Company will not be offering a scrip dividend alternative. However, the Company offers the option for shareholders to invest their dividend in a Dividend Reinvestment Plan ("DRIP"). Further details on the DRIP, can be found on the Registrar's website here -  Dividend Reinvestment Plan (computershare.com).

The last date for receipt for elections for the Dividend Reinvestment Plan is 2 October 2026.

data.title: Polish central banker Zarzecki sees rates on hold, warns of 2027 hike risk
data.description:
Key points:
  • Polish MPC's Zarzecki says rates may stay on hold until year-end
  • Zarzecki says rate hike in Q1 2027 is possible
  • Zarzecki sees risk from loose fiscal policy

By Pawel Florkiewicz

Polish interest rates could remain unchanged until the end of this year, though a first-quarter 2027 hike cannot be ruled out if a commodities shock has a lasting impact on inflation, central banker Marcin Zarzecki told Reuters.

The National Bank of Poland kept its main interest rate at 3.75% last week, maintaining its cautious approach as rising commodity prices and increased energy costs create a risk of higher inflation.

After that, NBP Governor Adam Glapinski said Poland's central bank was in wait-and-see mode, and interest rates may remain unchanged until the middle of next year.

"If the situation remained as it is currently, interest rates could stay unchanged until the end of the year, with a hike possible in the first quarter of 2027," Zarzecki said in an interview.

The Monetary Policy Council member outlined three scenarios for monetary policy, all centred on developments in commodity markets and their impact on inflation.

In the first scenario, a temporary rise in commodity prices lifts inflation towards the end of 2026 before price growth slows and stabilises slightly above 3%.

"In such an environment, the Council may keep interest rates unchanged for some time this year and next, while monitoring whether the rise in CPI remains a supply-side phenomenon," Zarzecki said.

Under an optimistic scenario, oil prices fall, geopolitical tensions ease and inflation returns to the central bank's 2.5% target after a temporary spike. In that case, interest rate cuts next year could not be ruled out, he said.

In a third scenario, which Zarzecki said was quite likely, high energy prices and a fuel shock feed through to transport costs, goods and services prices, and inflation expectations.

"This is a threshold the Council must monitor very closely, and under this scenario, an interest rate hike should be considered," he said.

Zarzecki said all three scenarios were plausible, though the first and third currently appeared the most likely.

INFLATION PATH

According to the NBP's short-term forecast, inflation could rise to around 4% in December 2026, remain close to 3.9% in January and February 2027, fall to about 3.2% in March and then climb again to 4.3% in June 2027.

"This does not mean that inflation has spiralled out of control again. However, neither does it mean that the inflation problem has been resolved," Zarzecki said.

Core inflation should remain in the 3.1%-3.4% range in coming months and hover around 3.3% in the first half of 2027, he added.

FISCAL POLICY

He also said the central bank must take into account the government's loose fiscal policy.

"If the central bank attempts to curb demand-side pressure and bring inflation down to its target while the public finance sector generates strong demand stimulus, the disinflation process may take longer," he said.

"A high deficit boosts demand, intensifies wage pressure, increases borrowing needs, affects bond yields and limits the scope for easing monetary policy."

data.title: ZAWYA: Ugandan coffee farmers take the heat from climate change
data.description:
By Staff Writer

Severe drought, a spike in coffee theft cases and fresh demand for Arabica coffee beans driven by Middle East, US and Chinese consumers widely shaped sentiment within Uganda’s coffee industry mid this year amid a weak production outlook blamed on depressed crop fields.

Wilted coffee trees dot dusty farms due to months of little rain, leaving many farmers stranded with poor harvests.

Increased reports of coffee theft in farms and homes have raised questions about farm security. While police reports routinely document livestock theft cases, coffee theft is not captured. Rising cases of coffee theft in farms, loss of harvested coffee beans in domestic stores, and limited police intervention pose a big headache to affected coffee farmers.

Average national coffee prices fell to Ush13,000 ($3.3) per kilogramme of Fair Average Coffee by close of August 2026, compared with a record high of Ush24,000 ($6) per kilogramme registered mid 2024, according to industry data.

Total monthly coffee exports recorded in June amounted to 744,540 60kg bags, valued at $175.5 million, government data shows. The export volumes comprised of 668,216 bags of Robusta coffee beans and 76,324 bags of Arabica coffee beans while the global market price averaged $3.9 per kilogramme by end of June 2026.

But coffee export volumes dropped by 14.9 percent to 846,376, 60 kilogramme bags valued at $204.1 million in July 2026, compared to July 2025. The export volumes were composed of 775,148 bags of Robusta coffee beans valued at $177.9 million and 71,228 bags of Arabica coffee beans valued at $26.1 million.

The United States of America ordered 10,401 60kg bags of Arabica coffee beans in July 2026 out of a total export volume of Arabica coffee estimated at 71,228, 60kg bags recorded during the same period.

The volume of Arabica coffee beans exported to China stood at 2,991 bags during the same period under review. In comparison, Saudi Arabia ordered 1,280 bags of Arabica coffee beans while Lebanon ordered 350 bags of Arabica coffee beans from the Ugandan market during July 2026, official figures revealed.

Eus Arinaitwe, a local coffee farmer based in western Uganda, said this season has been the hardest due to intense heat which forced the government to allocate solar irrigation pumps.“Irrigation helped rescue some of my coffee trees that I planted quite late but the flowering does not look good. The weight of coffee beans might also be affected by the intense heat and this will affect harvest volumes this year. The growing coffee theft cases are inspired by a single fact; coffee is the easiest commodity to sell because of a ready market, and the price still looks nice despite the huge drop. For example, 100 kilogrammes of coffee are enough to realise more than Ush1 million ($255) in this market at a price of Ush13, 000($3.3) per kilogramme at this time,” he said.

Coffee exports generated $1.5 billion by close of May 2026, compared with $2.5 billion recorded from labour remittances and $3 billion raised from gold exports during the same period, a scenario that consolidates the coffee sector’s position among the country’s leading forex earners.
